about: Reviewed expected-divergence list of the issue #196 differential fuzz, keyed by case id. ts/tests/differential.test.ts accepts a divergence only when its case id is listed here with its issue and exactly the symptom observed (`ts=<this runtime's answer> ref=<the reference's>`, each refusal with its class or code, a value mismatch with a digest of this runtime's values); it fails on any other divergence, on a listed case that no longer diverges so, and on any case the reference did not judge. No rule attributes a divergence: each entry was triaged by hand. `side` says which side is wrong (reference, runtime), or that the runtime differs by a decision settled on the issue (decision), or that the issue awaits the owner's call (owner-call). `cases` and `skipped` are rewritten by UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 npm test, which keeps an entry only while its id and symptom are unchanged and writes any other divergence unclassified (issue 0) for review.

issues.102: Settled decisions 7 and 8 of #102: schemaFromContract does not verify the identities hashes (canonicalization is candid-core's job) and does not read producer metadata (untrusted provenance); Contract::from_json refuses a document whose identities or producer block is wrong. The driver restamps identities after any graph edit, so only an edit of identities or producer itself diverges.
issues.103: Settled decisions of #103. Decision 4: the runtime refuses a non-minimal LEB128/SLEB128 group (overlong_leb128, or invalid_length when a u32 field's group is longer than five bytes although its value fits), the candid crate accepts it; triage: each generated case agrees with the reference once the runtime's minimality checks are reversed (and nothing else). Scope item 3 ("Bounded: input byte ceilings, type-table size caps, recursion depth, element-count limits — explicit, fail-closed"): the decoder has explicit budgets the candid crate does not have — maxBytes 10,485,760, maxDepth 256, maxElements 1,000,000 and maxNumericBytes 1,048,576 for one nat or int — so a message one past them is refused here and accepted there: the boundary vectors past maxDepth on the skip paths with no rec hop involved (skip_field_vec_256_levels, absorbed_vec_256_levels, depth_reserved_arg_vec_257_levels, skip_extra_arg_vec_258_levels, skip_extra_arg_record_vec_258_levels, skip_extra_arg_opt_258_levels, skip_extra_arg_variant_258_levels), past maxElements (elements_skipped_vec_1000000, elements_skipped_vec_variant_500000, elements_skipped_vec_record_500000, elements_decoded_vec_null_500000, elements_blob_999999, elements_mixed_vec_45453_pad_18), past maxBytes (bytes_text_message_10485761) and past maxNumericBytes (numeric_nat_1048577_groups, numeric_int_1048577_groups). Random generation stays far below each.
issues.104: Settled decision 1 of #104: a func value's method name is non-empty (the runtime's decode refuses an empty one with invalid_length, for round-trip symmetry with validate and encode; the candid crate accepts it), and opaque references and external reference sequences stay refused (a future value with a non-zero reference count: invalid_principal). Triage: each generated case agrees once the runtime's empty-name check is reversed (and nothing else).
issues.227: Upstream defects of the candid crate 0.10.30, found by this fuzz; the reference is wrong in each listed case and the runtime is right: wire-side-only empty normalization (item 1), values read from an empty wire type (item 2), the unsound coinductive subtype memo (item 3), a skipped func reference's method name not checked for UTF-8 (item 4). Each case is a hand-minimized vector with its analysis in regressions.json.
issues.228: schemaFromContract accepts Contract documents Contract::from_json refuses: orphan type nodes (item 7), unknown keys (item 6), a rootless arena (item 8); the runtime's loader is the wrong side. Item 9 (a document without declarations, which the runtime refuses and the reference accepts) awaits the owner's call. Triage: the reference's first violation names the rule, and the runtime's loader has no such check.
issues.229: Field names attach to the shared canonical node, so a declaration that spells a field by number (or another name) is decoded and validated under another declaration's spelling (d for 100, y for 121); the owner's question on #229. Triage: each decode case's values equal the reference's once every key and tag is read as its label id; each validate case's value uses the declaration's own spelling.
issues.231: The runtime charges a rec hop a step (#231): decode and validate refuse the first decoded node at Candid level 128 (257 steps) where the candid crate (no depth budget) accepts, and validate's tag-only arm is charged its rec hop but not its null, one level unlike candid-core's max_value_depth (the boundary vectors past maxDepth on the decoded paths, the path of coercion-inserted opts, and an expected reserved field, whose rec hop moves the bound by one wire level). The same step charges an element too, so validate reaches maxElements well before candid-core's max_value_elements counts as many HostValue nodes (validate_elements_record_vec_null_499998: 1,000,001 runtime steps, 500,000 HostValue nodes; validate_elements_mixed_vec_34481_pad_22); #231 states the depth half, and the element half is reported to the lead to add there. Random generation stays strictly below these bounds; only these exact boundary vectors cross them. Owner's call on #231.
issues.235: Contract::from_json accepts a struct written as a JSON array (serde's sequence form), e.g. a record field or a declaration; schemaFromContract refuses it (invalid_contract_document). Whether the format admits the sequence form is the owner's call (#235); candid-core writes objects only.
